findings.problem: These `@[simp]` lemmas mention `mulSingle` or `Pi.mulSingle`, which take a `[DecidableEq ι]` argument. Because of `open scoped Classical in`, the statements fix `Classical.propDecidable` as the instance instead of quantifying over it. A simp lemma stated this way only fires when the goal uses that same instance. It will not fire for an `ι` with its own instance (`ℕ`, `Fin n`, `ZMod n`) or for a `[DecidableEq ι]` section variable. Mathlib's `mulSingle`, `mulSingle_eq_of_ne` and `Pi.mulSingle` lemmas are all generic in the instance. The same fixed instance shows up in the in-file call sites, where the simp lemmas are passed by name even though they are already `@[simp]`: `simpa [structureMapMonoidHom_pi_mulSingle]` and `simp [z, u, hi, finset_prod_mulSingle_apply]`.
findings.proposed_change: State `structureMapMonoidHom_pi_mulSingle` and `finset_prod_mulSingle_apply` with a `variable [DecidableEq ι]` instead of `open scoped Classical in`. The proofs should not need the classical instance, since they only use `by_cases`, `Pi.mulSingle` and `Finset.prod_eq_single_of_mem`. Make `coordinateCharacter` take `[DecidableEq ι]` and use `mulSingleMonoidHom U i` directly, so that `coordinateCharacter_apply` and `reconstructedCoordinate_spec` become instance-generic. Keep `classical` only inside the main proofs. Then drop the redundant explicit simp arguments at lines 259, 279 and 280.
findings.benefit: The normal form `χ (mulSingle U i x)` would be reachable by plain `simp` for any decidable index type. Callers would not need to supply the classical instance or restate the lemmas by name. This also matches the generic style of Mathlib's `mulSingle` API.

findings.problem: `characterTestSet` has no membership lemma, and it is defined by a tactic block that fixes a classical `mulSingle`. Proofs that use it therefore unfold it by hand. At lines 378 and 386 they build membership with `Or.inl ⟨u, rfl⟩` and `Or.inr (Set.mem_iUnion_of_mem i <| Set.mem_iUnion_of_mem hi ⟨x, rfl⟩)`. This reveals the internal union/range shape and breaks if the definition changes. There are no canonical rewrite rules, so `simp` cannot reduce `z ∈ characterTestSet U s`.
findings.proposed_change: Add lemmas such as `range_structureMap_subset_characterTestSet` and `range_mulSingle_subset_characterTestSet`, or a membership iff `z ∈ characterTestSet U s ↔ z ∈ Set.range (structureMapMonoidHom U) ∨ ∃ i ∈ s, z ∈ Set.range (mulSingle U i)`. Mark the iff `@[simp]`, or at least `mem_characterTestSet`, and use it at lines 378 and 386 in place of the raw `Or.inl` / `Or.inr` terms.
findings.benefit: The proof of `continuous_toPontryaginDualMulEquiv_symm` would no longer depend on the internal shape of the definition. Future uses would have a canonical way to enter and leave `characterTestSet`.
